description: Default architecture, no weight assignment (random init, expected ~0% accuracy).
1-layer 8-dim hand circuit: attention counts ones (k-1 in a dim), LN made near-linear by a constant channel, 20 ReLU units compute parity via sum_j (-1)^(j+1)[k>=j]. (2000 samples only.)

1-layer 8-dim hand circuit: attention counts ones (k-1 in a dim), LN made near-linear by a constant channel, 10 ReLUs compute parity as a triangle wave relu(k)+sum_j 2(-1)^j relu(k-j). (2000 samples only.)
Same triangle-wave circuit as v2 but d_model=6 (dropping the two unused residual dims): 1 layer, 10 ReLUs. (2000 samples only.)
v3 with the positional embedding removed (it was all zeros); attention is uniform and needs no position info. 1 layer, d_model=6, 10 ReLUs. (2000 samples only.)
v4 with the constant channel reduced from C=139 to C=54 (sigma=12) to test how much LayerNorm nonlinearity the circuit tolerates. (2000 samples only.)
v5 with C reduced to 9 (sigma=3): stress test of the LayerNorm-linearity assumption; expected to degrade. (2000 samples only.)
d_model=5: the is-'1' and is-'=' flags are merged into one dim (+1 for '1', -1 for '='), since the count is still linear in the sum; C=53. Fails; cause not diagnosed.

d_model=5 with the is-'1'/is-'=' flags merged into one dim, and C=139 to shrink the LayerNorm1 per-token bias (diagnosis test for v7, which used C=53 and got 51.85%). Same accuracy, so the bias was not the cause.
Ablation: v4 circuit (D=6, no pos emb, C=139) with only 9 ReLU units (j=0..8). Expected to fail on counts k=10 (all-ones inputs).
v4 circuit (D=6, no pos emb, C=139, 10 ReLUs) re-checked on 300k samples; the 9-unit ablation misses the all-ones (k=10) case, so the 10th unit is needed.
Ablation: v10 circuit with 8 ReLU units (j=0..7); expected to fail on counts k>=9.
Ablation: v10 circuit with 6 ReLU units (j=0..5); expected to fail on counts k>=7.
Ablation: v10 circuit with 5 ReLU units (j=0..4).
Ablation: v10 circuit with 4 ReLU units (j=0..3).
Ablation: v10 circuit with 3 ReLU units (j=0..2).
v10 circuit (10 ReLUs, no pos emb) with C=54 instead of 139, re-evaluated on 300k samples.
v10 circuit (10 ReLUs, no pos emb) with C=24 (sigma=6), 300k samples.
v10 circuit (10 ReLUs, no pos emb) with C=9 (sigma=3), 300k samples.
v10 circuit (10 ReLUs, no pos emb) with C=4 (sigma=2), 300k samples.
v10 circuit (10 ReLUs, no pos emb) with C=2 (sigma=1.6), 300k samples.
No LayerNorm anywhere (Identity), d_model=5 (is-1, is-=, count, P, 1-P), exact linear count then 10 ReLUs as a triangle wave. Exact (no LN approximation).
v21 without the 1-P dimension: d_model=4, head logit('1')=P and logit('0')=0, relying on argmax tie-breaking to output '0' at P=0.
Ablation: exact d_model=3 circuit (is-1, count=k, P) with 9 ReLUs (j=0..8); misses all-ones k=10 inputs.
Ablation: exact d_model=3 circuit with 8 ReLUs (j=0..7).

Ablation: exact d_model=3 circuit with 2 ReLUs (j=0..1).

Exact d_model=3 circuit (is-1, count=k, P) with 10 ReLUs: no '=' flag needed since the count is exactly k; thresholds relu(k-j) with bias -j; head logit('1')=P. Best and most interpretable; 300k samples.
